task:
Explore: body-count filter pop-out (18 sliders) and a refresh-safe "search near" anchor.

Owner requests (2026-11-01). Read docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design.md (F4 rules, flag VITE_FINDER_F4_ENABLED, which is ON in governed release builds since #974) and the current apps/web/src/lib/features/explore code on main (Explore now stays empty until a search is requested, #975).

PART A — anchor in the URL so a refresh keeps the search.
Today the "search near" anchor lives only in SvelteKit page state, so a reload drops it while ?selected survives. Add a bounded `near=<id64>` URL parameter (lossless id64 string, validated like other ids) that is written whenever an anchor is committed (autocomplete choice, history) and removed when it is cleared. On load, a `near` parameter restores the anchor: resolve its name and coordinates through the existing lookup (the same path the selected-point reconstruction uses) or the autocomplete/system facade, and treat it as results intent so the list loads. Keep page-state anchors working for history, but the URL is now the source of truth on reload and in shared links. Invalid/unresolvable `near` values canonicalize away with a short notice, never a crash. A plain /explore load must still issue no results request.

PART B — body-count filters (owner chose these over weight sliders; there is no weight-slider work).
1. A "Body filters" button next to the archetype picker opens a pop-out window (non-modal dialog; Escape, Close and an outside click close it; focus returns to the trigger; centred sheet under ~640px wide; panel max-height limited to the visible viewport like the planner facility pop-up in SystemPane.svelte). Tabs: Planets, Stars, Features, each with a count badge.
2. Sliders, each a min/max range of whole counts with paired number inputs and an "Any" (no maximum) state, with accessible names:
   Planets: Earth-like (elw_count), Water worlds (ww_count), Ammonia worlds (ammonia_count), Terraformable (terraformable_count), Gas giants (gas_giant_count), High metal content (hmc_count), Metal-rich (metal_rich_count), Rocky (rocky_count), Rocky ice (rocky_ice_count), Icy (icy_count).
   Stars: Black holes (black_hole_count), Neutron stars (neutron_count), White dwarfs (white_dwarf_count), Other stars (other_star_count).
   Features: Landable (landable_count), Walkable (walkable_count), Rings (ring_count), Biological signals (bio_signal_total), Geological signals (geo_signal_total).
   The keys are exactly BodyFilters in apps/api/src/models.py, sent as LocalSearchRequest.body_filters {key: {min?, max?}} on POST /api/local/search through the generated client/facade (searchExploreSystems in apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts). Choose sensible slider maxima per type (for example 0–20 for most planet types, 0–50 for landable, 0–10 for stars); typing a larger number than the slider maximum is allowed up to a hard bound of 999. Omit a key when it is unset; never send min > max.
3. Footer: "N filters selected", Reset (clears the draft), Cancel (discards the draft), Apply (commits). Nothing is requested while dragging; one search per Apply.
4. Applied filters show as removable chips above the results ("Earth-like ≥ 1", "Landable 2–5", "Rings ≤ 3") with "Clear all". Removing a chip or clearing re-runs the search once.
5. Filters live in the URL (owner rule 2026-11-01: link only, never local storage): a bounded `bodies` parameter, for example `bodies=elw_count:1-,landable_count:2-5`, parsed fail-closed (unknown keys, non-integers, negative values or min > max are dropped by canonicalization like other invalid Explore parameters).
6. Scope: body filters apply to the near-a-system search only (they need the anchor). When an archetype other than Any is selected (the /api/archetypes/rankings path, which has no body_filters), the button is disabled with the explanation "Body filters work when you search near a system." and any applied filters stay in the URL but show as paused chips. With no anchor and Any, the button is also disabled with the same explanation.
7. Work with the F4 flag on and off; with it off, the anchor and filters still work for the legacy near-system search.

Tests: Vitest for URL parse/serialize (near and bodies, including fail-closed cases), the pop-out (tabs, sliders, number inputs, Any, Reset/Cancel/Apply, focus return, Escape/outside click, visible-viewport height), chips and Clear all, the disabled states, one request per Apply, and a reload restoring both anchor and filters. Cypress product-journey.cy.ts: choose an anchor, open Body filters, set Earth-like ≥ 1, apply, assert the request body's body_filters and the URL, reload and assert the list and chips come back, run axe on the open pop-out; keep intercept aliases unique. Also update apps/web/cypress/e2e/review-lab.cy.ts only if it is affected (the Review Lab API has no /api/v1/generation or /api/v1/systems routes, so Review Lab flows must not depend on them). Add a CHANGES.md entry. Run pnpm check, pnpm test and pnpm build in apps/web.
